title: Smallest Good Base
description: Given a decimal integer `n` represented as a string (`3 <= n <= 10^18`), return the smallest good base `k` (`k >= 2`) as a string. An integer `k >= 2` is called a good base of `n` if every digit of `n` when written in base `k` is `1` (meaning `n = 1 + k + k^2 + ... + k^m` for some integer `m >= 1`).
constraints: n is a decimal integer string in the range [3, 10^18].
n does not contain leading zeros.
hints: A smaller base `k` corresponds to more `1`-digits `m + 1`, so test `m` from `floor(log2(n))` down to `2`; the first valid base found is guaranteed to be the smallest (otherwise `m = 1` gives `k = n - 1`).
For each fixed `m`, binary search `k` in `[2, n - 1]` and evaluate `1 + k + ... + k^m` with overflow-safe checks (`term > (n - sum) // k`) to avoid 64-bit integer overflow.

examples.explanation: 13 in base 3 is 111 (1 + 3 + 9 = 13), so 3 is the smallest good base.
10^18 has no good base with 3 or more digits, so its smallest good base is 10^18 - 1 (giving "11").
